graphql_request.description: Send a query or mutation to any GraphQL API that Lodol has no built-in step for. Write the query as in the API's own explorer, fill in its variables, and the data comes back ready for later steps to read, with any errors the API reported. Store an API token as a workspace secret and reference it in a header.
graphql_request.name: graphql_request

parameters.description: The GraphQL endpoint, starting with https://, such as https://api.github.com/graphql. It can be built from workspace values.
parameters.name: url

parameters.description: The query or mutation to send, written in GraphQL. Declare the values that change as variables, such as query ($id: ID!), and set them below rather than writing them into the query.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: A value for each variable the query declares, named without the dollar sign. A value can be a reference to an earlier step, or JSON for an object or a list. Put text that looks like a number in quotes, such as "12345".
parameters.name: variables

parameters.description: Which operation to run when the query holds more than one. Leave it empty for a query with a single operation.
parameters.name: operation_name

parameters.description: Headers to send, such as an Authorization header. Use a workspace secret for a token so it is never stored in the workflow.
parameters.name: headers

parameters.description: What an error means for this step: an error status (a 401, a 500) or a reply whose errors list is not empty. Treating them as results lets later steps read the errors themselves and use any data that did come back. A request that gets no answer at all still fails the step; the step's own "If this step fails" setting decides what happens then.
parameters.name: on_error

request.description: Call any REST or GraphQL endpoint that Lodol has no built-in step for. Set the method, URL, headers, query parameters, and body, and the response comes back ready for later steps to read. Store an API token as a workspace secret and reference it in a header to make an authenticated call.
request.name: request

parameters.description: The full address to call, starting with https://. It can be built from workspace values, for example @values.BASE_URL followed by the path.
parameters.name: url

parameters.description: The HTTP method the endpoint expects.
parameters.name: method

parameters.description: Headers to send, such as an Authorization header. Use a workspace secret for a token so it is never stored in the workflow.
parameters.name: headers

parameters.description: Values added to the end of the URL as a query string. Anything already written into the URL is kept.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: What to send with the request, as JSON or a reference to a value from an earlier step. Leave it empty for a request that carries no body, such as a GET.
parameters.name: body

parameters.description: How to encode the body. JSON suits most APIs, including GraphQL. Form sends it the way an HTML form would. Multipart uploads files: each field of the body is text, or a file from an upload or an earlier step.
parameters.name: body_format

parameters.description: How to read what comes back. Auto follows the response's own content type, so JSON becomes an object and a download becomes a file.
parameters.name: response_format

parameters.description: What an error status (a 404, a 500) means for this step. Treating it as a result lets later steps check the status themselves, which suits a 404 that just means not found. A request that gets no answer at all still fails the step; the step's own "If this step fails" setting decides what happens then.
parameters.name: on_error

parameters.description: Log in as one of the workspace's connections (a Salesforce, Google or Notion account, ...), which adds that account's credentials for you. For calling an endpoint of a connected app that its actions don't cover. The request can only go to that app's own servers.
parameters.name: connection_id

parameters.description: Pick the type your API's docs describe.
parameters.name: paging

parameters.description: The field in each response that holds the list, like data. Leave empty if the response is the list.
parameters.name: paging_items

parameters.description: The field in each response that holds the next page's link or cursor, like links.next.
parameters.name: paging_next

parameters.description: The URL parameter that asks for a page, like page or cursor.
parameters.name: paging_param

parameters.description: Stops here even if there are more pages.
parameters.name: paging_max_pages

has_more.description: Whether the page cap stopped it early.

pages.description: How many pages were fetched, when paging.

description: Call any REST or GraphQL endpoint.
